text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwean taxpayers will be forced to pay Z$150 million annually for the next decade to finance loan repayments for the Z$1.2 billion new terminal at Harare International Airport, official sources said on Wednesday.

- One of the losing bidders for Zimbabwe's second cellular phone licence, Econet, on Wednesday filed an application in the High Court seeking to be granted a licence as the firm's boss said he would not part with the Z$100 million phone equipment he had already acquired for the project.

- Zimbabwe's customs and excise department this week introduced a series of new measures designed to widen the government's revenue base and curb fraud by importers and exporters who illegally dump goods in Zimbabwe on the pretext of transiting the country.

- The Methodist Church in Zimbabwe said this week it had set up a committee of senior church leaders to interview former state president Banana, a minister of the church, on widely publicised allegations he sodomised his former aide-de-camp.

- Zimbabwe's second private airliner, Expedition Airways, is expected to start operations within the next few weeks following the granting of a long-awaited authorisation by the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe last week.
- Pharmaceutical manufacturer CAPS Holdings has successfully raised Z$55 million in loan finance, most of which will be used to retire its more expensive debt.
- The country's sole coal producer, Wankie, is losing out on the lucrative export market due to exhorbitant transport costs which are higher than the actual price of the mineral.

- Fourteen African heads of state and government have so far confirmed their participation at the 33rd meeting of leaders of countries in the Organisation of African Unity to be held in Harare early next month.

- A critical shortage of vehicles has hit Harare Fire Brigade's ambulance section with only eight currently serving the city and hampering the department's capability to respond to health emergencies.
